messages:
Anna (support): FYI - customer ACME hitting intermittent failures on /v1/rerank. Sometimes a 400 with "invalid input", other times we return a list of identical scores (0.0, 0.0, ...). They included payloads with emojis and some � characters.
Miguel (eng): Can you drop a minimal repro payload here?
Anna (support): Sure, sample from their POST body:
```json
{
  "query": "find rune sequence 🔣�",
  "documents": ["normal doc", "weird 𐀀 sequence", "emoji cluster 😂😂"]
}
```
Anna (support): They said ~2% of rerank calls fail, mostly on batches containing mixed emoji + embedded nulls.
Riya (ml): I pulled logs for x-request-id=acme-7f9e. Runtime shows malformed UTF-8 hitting tokenizer and bubbling up as a 500 in some cases:```
[2026-11-06T14:02:11Z] ERROR model_infer.cc:142 invalid_utf8_sequence at offset 27
[2026-11-06T14:02:11Z] WARN rerank_service.cc:89 fallback_scores_all_equal
```
Riya (ml): The � seems to cause the tokenizer to produce empty tokens and our scoring path ends up returning degenerate logits in some quantized kernels.
Ken (sre): What headers/curl did they use? maybe content-type mismatch or double-encoding?
Anna (support): They used curl via an internal proxy. Repro by curl:```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8' \
  -d @payload.json
```
Miguel (eng): Quick triage suggestions: 1) Return 422 with clear error when control characters detected, 2) Add server-side sanitizer that strips NULs and replaces invalid sequences with U+FFFD before tokenization, 3) Add a unit test that asserts we never hit quantized-kernel edge case with empty token lists.
Riya (ml): Agree. Short-term we should reject and give customers actionable message. Longer-term, do controlled sanitization + telemetry for how often it happens.
ACME Ops (customer): Thanks, we're blocked on a small % of traffic — can you share ETA for a fix? :pray:
Anna (support): Apologies for the disruption. We're triaging now and will push a config change to return 422 within the hour if the control-character detector fires. I'll follow up with an incident ticket and ETA.
Ken (sre): Created internal incident: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-432 (OpsBot recorded). Escalating to eng-ml and eng-runtime.
OpsBot: Incident INC-2026-432 acknowledged by @Riya.
Miguel (eng): I'll open a GH issue for the sanitizer/hotfix and add the failing sample as a test. GH#: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank/issues/845 (placeholder).
Riya (ml): After hotfix, we should schedule an eval to ensure no regression on tokenization and a canary rollout to Dedicated customers.
Anna (support): I'll update ACME with the incident link + temporary mitigation. Will post here when hotfix is live. :white_check_mark:
